title: SB 79 (2025): transit-oriented housing development
codified: Gov. Code §§ 65912.155–65912.162 (Chapter 4.1.5 of Division 1 of Title 7)
readme: Every value is a cited leaf: value, cite (one pinpoint), source (snapshot file in source/), and quote (verbatim from that pinpoint). Leaves with from/to are in force on dates from <= d < to. A provision with versions lists each wording by date. test/citations.test.ts checks every quote against the official text.

effective.quote: Added by Stats. 2025, Ch. 512, Sec. 1. (SB 79) Effective January 1, 2026.
by Stats. 2026, Ch. 100, Sec. 2. (SB 722) Effective July 16, 2026.

sb722.amends: Gov. Code § 65912.157: adds (h)(3); corrects wording in (h) and (j). Urgency statute.

effective.quote: a statute enacted at a regular session shall go into effect on January 1 next following a 90-day period from the date of enactment of the statute

ab2576.amends: Gov. Code § 65912.161: rewrites (b)(1)(F); renumbers (c). Section 1 controls: Section 1.5 was conditioned on AB 2415, which was not enacted.

effective.quote: a statute enacted at a regular session shall go into effect on January 1 next following a 90-day period from the date of enactment of the statute

sb1361.amends: Gov. Code § 65912.157: splits (c) into (c)(1) and new (c)(2); corrects wording in (j).

cities.quote: This section shall not apply to a local agency until July 1, 2026

unincorporated.quote: It shall not apply within an unincorporated area of a county until the 7th regional housing needs allocation cycle.

urbanTransitCountyMoreThanRailStations.quote: means a county with more than 15 passenger rail stations
urbanTransitCountyMoreThanRailStations.note: Strictly more than 15. The statute lists no counties.

tier1.value: heavy rail transit or very high frequency commuter rail, in an urban transit county
tier1.quote: served by heavy rail transit or very high frequency commuter rail

tier2.value: light rail, high-frequency commuter rail, or bus service meeting Pub. Resources Code § 21060.2(a)(1), in an urban transit county
tier2.quote: served by light rail transit, by high-frequency commuter rail, or by bus service meeting the standards of paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) of Section 21060.2 of the Public Resources Code

veryHighFrequencyCommuterRailTrainsPerDa.quote: a total of at least 72 trains per day across both directions

highFrequencyCommuterRailTrainsPerDay.quote: operating a total of at least 48 trains per day across both directions

todZoneRadius.quote: means the area within one-half mile of a transit-oriented development stop

adjacentWithin.quote: means within 200 feet of any pedestrian access point to a transit-oriented development stop

highResourceArea.quote: an area designated as highest resource or high resource on the most recently adopted version of the opportunity area maps

housingDevelopmentProjectExcludesTransie.quote: does not include a project of which any portion is designated for use as a hotel, motel, bed and breakfast inn, or other transient lodging

netHabitableSquareFootage.value: finished and heated floor area with at least 6.5 ft headroom, excluding garages, carports, parking, cellars, half-stories, and unfinished attics and basements
netHabitableSquareFootage.quote: the finished and heated floor area fully enclosed by the inside surface of walls, windows, doors, and partitions

residentialFloorAreaRatio.value: net habitable square footage in residential use divided by lot area
residentialFloorAreaRatio.quote: means the ratio of net habitable square footage dedicated to residential use to the area of the lot

qualifyingZoning.quote: on any site zoned for residential, mixed, or commercial development

reach.quote: within one-half or one-quarter mile of a transit-oriented development stop

distanceMeasurement.value: straight line from the nearest edge of the parcel to a pedestrian access point of the stop
distanceMeasurement.quote: measured in a straight line from the nearest edge of the parcel containing the proposed project to a pedestrian access point for the transit-oriented development stop

tier1.quote: within a city with a population of at least 35,000
tier1.note: The statute does not say which population count or date applies.

tier2.quote: within a city with a population of at least 35,000
tier2.note: The statute does not say which population count or date applies.

tier1.quote: within one-quarter mile of a Tier 1 transit-oriented development stop

tier2.quote: within one-quarter mile of a Tier 2 transit-oriented development stop

tier1.quote: further than one-quarter mile but within one-half mile of a Tier 1 transit-oriented development stop

tier2.quote: further than one-quarter mile but within one-half mile of a Tier 2 transit-oriented development stop

heightLimitAtLeastFt.quote: shall not impose any height limit less than 75 feet

maxDensityAtLeastDuPerAcre.quote: shall not impose any maximum density of less than 120 dwelling units per acre

residentialFarNotPrecludedUpTo.quote: physically preclude achieving a residential floor area ratio of up to 3.5

concessionMinDensityDuPerAcre.quote: achieves a minimum density of 90 dwelling units per acre

heightLimitAtLeastFt.quote: shall not impose any height limit less than 65 feet

maxDensityAtLeastDuPerAcre.quote: shall not impose any maximum density standard of less than 100 dwelling units per acre

residentialFarNotPrecludedUpTo.quote: physically preclude achieving a residential floor area ratio of up to 3.

concessionMinDensityDuPerAcre.quote: achieves a minimum density of 75 dwelling units per acre

heightLimitAtLeastFt.quote: shall not impose any height limit less than 65 feet

maxDensityAtLeastDuPerAcre.quote: shall not impose any maximum density standard of less than 100 dwelling units per acre

residentialFarNotPrecludedUpTo.quote: physically preclude achieving a residential floor area ratio of up to 3.

concessionMinDensityDuPerAcre.quote: achieves a minimum density of 75 dwelling units per acre

heightLimitAtLeastFt.quote: shall not impose any height limit less than 55 feet

maxDensityAtLeastDuPerAcre.quote: shall not impose any maximum density standard of less than 80 dwelling units per acre

residentialFarNotPrecludedUpTo.quote: physically preclude achieving a residential floor area ratio of up to 2.5

concessionMinDensityDuPerAcre.quote: achieves a minimum density of 60 dwelling units per acre

appliesTo.value: a qualifying project immediately adjacent to the stop (within 200 feet of a pedestrian access point, § 65912.156(a))
appliesTo.quote: is immediately adjacent to a transit-oriented development stop shall be eligible for an adjacency intensifier

heightAddFt.quote: increase the height limit by an additional 20 feet

densityAddDuPerAcre.quote: the maximum density standard by an additional 40 dwelling units per acre

residentialFarAdd.quote: the residential floor area ratio by 1 prior to the application of Section 65915

minUnits.quote: shall include at least five dwelling units

minDensityDuPerAcre.quote: A minimum density of at least 30 dwelling units per acre.

localMinDensityIfGreater.value: the minimum density required under local zoning, if greater
localMinDensityIfGreater.quote: The minimum density required under local zoning, if applicable.

maxAverageUnitSizeNetSqFt.quote: shall not exceed 1,750 net habitable square feet

safety.value: consistent with airport land use compatibility plans, military AICUZ, and objective fire safety standards
safety.quote: shall be consistent with the height, noise, and safety standards of an adopted airport land use compatibility plan

appliesAboveUnits.quote: This paragraph shall not apply to any development of 10 units or less.

extremelyLow.quote: At least 7 percent of the total units

veryLow.quote: At least 10 percent of the total units

lower.quote: At least 13 percent of the total units

rentalTermYears.quote: all affordable rental units included pursuant to this section for 55 years

ownershipTermYears.quote: all affordable ownership units included pursuant to this section for a period of 45 years

stricterLocalInclusionaryControls.quote: the local inclusionary housing requirement mandate shall apply in place of the requirements in paragraph (1)

replacementHousing.value: comply with Gov. Code § 66300.6 (replacement of demolished protected units)

localDemolitionStandards.value: comply with applicable local demolition and antidisplacement ordinances
localDemolitionStandards.quote: shall comply with any applicable local demolition and antidisplacement standards established through a local ordinance

moreThanUnits.quote: A site containing more than two units where the development would require the demolition of housing that is subject to any form of rent or price control

tenantLookbackYears.quote: that has been occupied by tenants within the past seven years

moreThanUnits.quote: A site that was previously used for more than two units of housing

lookbackYears.quote: that were demolished within seven years before the development proponent submits an application

parkSite.value: mobilehome, RV, or special occupancy park sites are barred
parkSite.quote: The existing parcel of land or site is governed under the Mobilehome Residency Law

buildingHeightOverFt.quote: for any building over 85 feet in height

standards.value: Gov. Code § 65913.4(a)(8)(A)–(D), (F), (G) (prevailing wage; skilled and trained workforce)
standards.quote: shall meet the labor standards of subparagraphs (A), (B), (C), (D), (F), and (G) of paragraph (8) of subdivision (a) of Section 65913.4

baseDensity.value: the SB 79 density is the base density for the Density Bonus Law
baseDensity.quote: using the density allowed under this section as the base density

noAdditionalHeightRequired.quote: shall not be required to grant a waiver, incentive, or concession pursuant to Section 65915 for additional height beyond that specified in this section

roundingRule.value: density bonus calculations round fractional units up
roundingRule.quote: All density calculations resulting in fractional units shall be rounded up to the next whole number.
roundingRule.note: Governs density bonus calculations; Chapter 4.1.5 has no rounding rule of its own for the base standards.

heightExceptionFt.quote: a height increase of up to three additional stories, or 33 feet
heightExceptionFt.note: For projects meeting § 65915(b)(1)(G) (100 percent lower income, up to 20 percent moderate) within one-half mile of a major transit stop.

extremelyLow.quote: For a development providing housing for extremely low income households, three additional concessions.

veryLow.quote: For a development providing housing for very low income households, two additional concessions.

low.quote: For a development providing housing for low-income households, one additional concession.

versions.value: local standards apply only if they do not, alone or in concert, prevent achieving the SB 79 standards
versions.quote: may still enact and enforce standards, including an inclusionary zoning requirement that do not, alone or in concert, prevent achieving the applicable development standards of subdivision (a)

versions.value: local standards apply only if they do not, alone or in concert, prevent achieving the SB 79 standards
versions.quote: may still enact and enforce standards, including an inclusionary zoning requirement that do not, alone or in concert, prevent achieving the applicable development standards of subdivision (a)

versions.value: no fees or requirements imposed because a project uses SB 79
versions.quote: applies to a project solely or partially on the basis that the project is seeking approval as a transit-oriented housing development

versions.value: no fees or requirements imposed because a project uses SB 79
versions.quote: applies to a project solely or partially on the basis that the project is seeking approval as a transit-oriented housing development

transitServiceProtections.value: a city may not seek transit cuts or hold up transit projects to avoid SB 79
transitServiceProtections.quote: A local government with an existing or planned transit-oriented development stop shall not do any of the following

deemedConsistent.quote: shall be deemed consistent, compliant, and in conformity with an applicable plan

noMinisterialProcessRequired.quote: This subdivision shall not require a ministerial approval process

ceqaUnchanged.quote: or modify the requirements of Division 13 (commencing with Section 21000) of the Public Resources Code

sb35Eligible.quote: shall be eligible for streamlined ministerial approval pursuant to Section 65913.4

conflictingZoningDoesNotApply.quote: any local zoning standard conflicting with the requirements of this chapter shall not apply

inHighResourceArea.quote: that is located in a high-resource area shall be presumed to be in violation of the Housing Accountability Act (Section 65589.5)

minFinePerUnitUsd.quote: The fine shall be in a minimum amount of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) per housing unit

mapPresumption.value: each MPO's map of TOD stops and zones is rebuttably presumed valid
mapPresumption.quote: This map shall have a rebuttable presumption of validity for use by project applicants and local governments.

draftDaysBeforeAdoption.quote: At least 14 days prior to adoption of an ordinance pursuant to this section

submitWithinDays.quote: to the department within 60 days of enactment

reviewDays.quote: The department shall, within 90 days, review the enacted ordinance

extensionDays.quote: the department may request an additional 30 days

noWalkingPathUnderMiles.quote: there exists no walking path of less than one mile from that location to the transit-oriented development stop

industrialHubMinStops.quote: A local government with at least 15 transit-oriented development stops designates the area as an industrial employment hub

industrialHubMinAcres.quote: a contiguous area of at least 250 acres

untilYearsAfterSeventhHousingElement.quote: Prior to one year following the adoption of the seventh revision of the housing element

versions.value: sites with a historic resource on a local register as of January 1, 2025
versions.quote: Sites with a historic resource designated as of January 1, 2025, on a local register.

versions.value: sites designated before January 1, 2025 on a local register or in the State Historic Resources Inventory
versions.quote: A contributing site within a historic district included on the State Historic Resources Inventory

sameTotalCapacity.quote: shall maintain at least the same total net zoned capacity, in terms of both total units and residential floor area

maxSiteDensityCutPercent.quote: by more than 50 percent below that permitted under this chapter

maxZoneCapacityCutPercent.quote: shall not reduce the capacity in any transit-oriented development zone in total units or residential floor area by more than 50 percent

maxSiteCapacityCountedPercent.quote: shall not exceed 200 percent of the maximum density established under this chapter

versions.value: a city may adopt an alternative plan deemed compliant by HCD under § 65912.160
versions.quote: may adopt an alternative plan that has been deemed compliant by the department pursuant to Section 65912.160

versions.value: a city may adopt an alternative plan deemed compliant by HCD under § 65912.160
versions.quote: may adopt an alternative plan that has been deemed compliant by the department pursuant to Section 65912.160

replacesDefaults.quote: Section 65912.157 shall not apply within a jurisdiction that has a local transit-oriented alternative plan that has been approved by the department
